name: footer_empty
reason: Wrong palette in src/widgets/footer-component.tsx: FOOTER_BACKGROUND is hardcoded to `#212B32`, but Python Textual's footer bar bg is `#242f38` (verified in visual-tests/snapshots/python/footer_empty.json — every cell on the bar row has background `#242f38`). xterm in Docker faithfully renders both colors; there is no truecolor rendering bug. Fix: change the constant. The earlier diagnosis (`xterm renders #212B32 as pure black`, with candidates around Ink's whitespace BG emission / xterm-direct terminfo / scroll-erase) was symptom-blaming — none of those candidates were verified, and consulting the Python baseline JSON immediately disproves them.

name: footer_with_bindings
reason:
Three independent palette/format gaps in src/widgets/footer-component.tsx and src/framework/app-framework.ts (verified against visual-tests/snapshots/python/footer_with_bindings.json):
  1. Bar background: JS `FOOTER_BACKGROUND = '#212B32'` vs Python `#242f38` (same as footer_empty).
  2. Chip key color: JS `FOOTER_KEY_COLOR = '#fea62b'` vs Python `#ffa62b` (typo: `fe` should be `ff`).
  3. Palette separator (`▏`) color: JS uses default fg `#e0e0e0` vs Python's dimmer `#495259`.
  4. Key formatting: JS `getKeyDisplay` emits `ctrl+r` vs Python's caret form `^r` — locatable in src/framework/app-framework.ts.
No truecolor/xterm rendering bug exists; the previous diagnosis was symptom-blaming.

name: input_focused
reason: NOT an Input rendering gap — Input focus styling is done and verified. `Input:focus` resolves border #0178d4, background #272727, placeholder #797979 and the reverse-video block cursor (#121212 on #e0e0e0); rendering the focused frame directly matches visual-tests/snapshots/python/input_focused.json at 240/240 cells, and tests/input-render.test.tsx asserts the focused frame differs from the blurred one. The blocker is framework key dispatch: postToFocused in src/framework/message-pump.ts (~line 305) drops the message when resolveDefaultDispatchTarget() returns undefined, and postKey (~line 313) routes every non-priority key through it. With AUTO_FOCUS = null (which this fixture sets, matching the Python fixture) nothing is focused, the Key message is discarded, and the app-level `{ key: 'tab', action: 'app.focus_next' }` binding at src/framework/_app-runtime.ts:459 never runs. Verified by probe: app.focusNext() focuses the Input correctly, but pilot.press('tab') leaves app.focusedNodeId null, and a custom app-level f5 binding does not fire either — no key reaches app bindings while nothing is focused. Textual routes unfocused keys to the Screen/App so app bindings still fire. Fix belongs in the framework, not in Input. Secondary, Input-side: handleInputKey in src/widgets/input-component.tsx calls message.stop() on every key including tab, so once focused the Input swallows Tab and focus cannot advance.
